newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: FOCUS-Manila shares likely to test new lows.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Manila shares likely to test new lows.

text.p: Manila shares fell for the fourth straight session on Tuesday, hitting a new 17-month low, and analysts said the market was likely to test even lower levels soon.
For the moment, however, the outlook depends on whether the United States decides to raise interest rates later on Tuesday.

"Everybody wants out of the market. They do not want to get stuck here before the FOMC (U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee) meets tonight," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Orion-Squire Capital Inc.
After an early spurt of buying, profit-taking pulled the main index down 9.98 points to close on Tuesday at 2,499.38.

"The minor rally was not sustained for the simple reason that investors are waiting for the (Philippine) GNP figures and the FOMC meeting," said Jidgette Valenzuela, research head at Lippo Securities.
Philippine gross national product data for the first quarter is due to be announced around the end of the month.
Traders said the market is likely to test the 2,450 support level on Wednesday for the first time since December 1995.

The stock market has been on a steep decline, shedding nearly 28 percent since falling off its all-time peak in February. Investors increasingly had worried that the problems of neighbouring Thailand would spill over into the Philippines.

"We've had a vicious fall. A lot of selling pressure has eased although foreign funds are still sceptical ahead of the FOMC and the release of first quarter gross national product figures," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities Phils Inc.

"We are still in the bottoming out process...But if U.S. rates are unchanged, there will be a little more confidence worldwide and maybe we will see this trickle down to the Philippines," said Raul Zamora, head of institutional sales at PCIBank Securities Inc.
Some said that no change in rates would be of little help to Manila stocks, however.

"I think even if the Fed leaves rates unchanged, if the Philippines is being compared to Thailand, people will still be extra cautious. There will have to be a lot of good news to reverse the trend. Perhaps a good first quarter GNP figure," said Felix Barrientos, dealer at ING Baring Securities.
Shrinking turnover indicates that any future fall of the market may not be as sharp as in recent days, he added.
Traders are hoping that a speech by President Fidel Ramos on Thursday in Hong Kong will encourage fund managers to return to Philippine shares.
"The President will be the number one salesman and if he plays it right, then it will be good for the market," said PCIBank's Zamora.
